\[
R_1 = I(x,y) - I(x+1,y+1),
\qquad
R_2 = I(x+1,y) - I(x,y+1)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(R_1, R_2\): The two diagonal differences

The two differences along the diagonals of the 2x2 block that starts at the pixel. Roberts used them in 1963, one of the first edge operators. Here they run as 3x3 kernels with the pixel at the center. The direction output is the angle of (R_1, R_2), which is the gradient angle turned by 45 degrees.
